newsitem.title: USA: Bell Atlantic to guide Iusacell.
newsitem.headline: Bell Atlantic to guide Iusacell.

text.p: Bell Atlantic Corp said it plans to use its experience to guide Grupo Iusacell SA de CV through the growing competition and opportunities of the Mexican telecommunications market.
"Iusacell needs more resources and more experience on a global basis to help them compete," said Brian Wood, corporate communications director for Bell Atlantic Enterprises.

The U.S. regional bell on Tuesday took management control of Iusacell via a capital reshuffle in which it kept its overall stake at 42 percent, but paid $50 million as a premium for control in both board seats and A class shares.
The 48 percent stake of the Peralta family remains unchanged, but the family will have the option to sell a third of its stake to Bell Atlantic over the next three years.
Iusacell began as a wireless company, but has grown into new areas just as new rivals have entered the market.
"They are facing a lot greater competition, people like MCI and AT&T with lots of money and big brand names," he said.
AT&T Corp entered Mexico through Alestra, a venture with Grupo Industrial Alfa, Valores Industriales, and Grupo Financiero Bancomer.
MCI Communications Corp has a venture called Avantel with the financial group Banamex-Accival.
All are positioning themselves for January 1, 1997 when the residential long distance monopoly of Telefonos de Mexico is ended.
To do so Iusacell, which had 225,000 customers at the end of the third quarter, has also entered new markets.
"Now they are moving into what you would call a full service network position, with cellular service, long distance, paging and wireless local loop," Wood told Reuters.
Wireless local loop provides conventional local telephone service, but without the expense of having to lay wires to a home or office. -- Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712
